inspiration: Biome as data: each biome file names its terrain types (gl_snow, gl_mountain, gl_desert, gl_meadow, gl_water) and points at one atlas for all of them (greenland.lua lines 46-74). Recreate a zone as a named terrain set that uses one texture atlas, with our own palette.

Upgrade as a second strip on the same atlas: the normal road and the upgraded road are two rows of one texture (greenland.lua lines 24 and 29). Recreate an upgrade cue as a second visual strip, so a tier change reads without a new asset.

Colour-keyed celebration bursts: the fireworks folder holds one burst sprite set per player slot (assets/base/fireworks/10.player.bmp and up, 32 files). Recreate a win burst as a per-team colour set, drawn with our own particles.
Missions as data-driven scripts with a version check and a TODO header (campaigns/roman/MISS200.lua). Recreate a mission as a data file with a version gate and a checklist of open items.

Faction as a full sprite family: a nation folder holds its own map, icon and job sprites (assets/nations/Babylonians). Recreate a faction's identity as its own silhouette set and icon family, never copying the existing sprites.

briefs.label: colour-keyed victory burst (own label)
briefs.why: Readable at 375 wide: a short burst in the winner's colour is one silhouette; one signature effect (a radial burst of sparks); one signature sound (a soft pop). Could be ours at 20-30 percent resemblance.
briefs.keep: per-player colour burst that fires on a win or milestone
briefs.change: particle burst instead of sprite frames, our own palette and a different burst shape. Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy
briefs.ref: data/RTTR/assets/base/fireworks/10.player.bmp (32 files in that folder; not opened, binary)

briefs.label: named biome terrain set (own label)
briefs.why: A biome is a readable palette and silhouette family at 375 wide. One signature behaviour: each terrain type has its own walkable rule in the data. Could be ours at 20-30 percent resemblance.
briefs.keep: a zone defined as a list of named terrain types that share one atlas
briefs.change: our own biome names, palette and terrain rules. Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy
briefs.ref: data/RTTR/gamedata/world/greenland.lua (lines 46-74 named terrain types); wasteland.lua and winterworld.lua (same pattern, not read)

briefs.label: upgrade strip on the road atlas (own label)
briefs.why: A tier change reads at a glance on a road tile; one signature effect is a second line drawn over the first. Could be ours at 20-30 percent resemblance.
briefs.keep: upgrade shown as a second strip of the same texture, no new file
briefs.change: a glow or dashed line instead of a stacked strip, our own colour. Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy
briefs.ref: data/RTTR/gamedata/world/greenland.lua lines 24 and 29 (pos entries for normal and upgraded road)

briefs.label: faction sprite family (own label)
briefs.why: A faction is identified by one silhouette family. One signature trait: its own icon set. Could be ours at 20-30 percent resemblance. Class C: category-level only
briefs.keep: a faction owns a full set of sprites, icon and map objects
briefs.change: our own silhouettes, proportions and icon style. Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy
